items.source_title: On-Behalf-Of: how agents act on a person's verified identity
items.short_factual_summary: Diagrid argues that agent service accounts create attribution and authorization gaps because downstream systems see only the agent identity, while on-behalf-of delegation keeps both the human subject and machine actor visible in short-lived scoped tokens.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is directly relevant to governed tool-call practice: agent actions should preserve requester identity, least privilege, and audit attribution across tool, MCP server, API, and agent-to-agent hops.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate source for a local delegated-agent-identity or approval-boundary lens; keep broad identity product coverage upstream.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, connect this to permission and audit-log pages rather than creating a local Diagrid product page.

items.source_title: Getting started with Ontraport's MCP Server
items.date_basis: Support page shows Last updated on: July 25, 2026.
items.short_factual_summary: Ontraport's MCP guidance warns that an agent has a bounded context window rather than full-database visibility, recommends direct APIs or workflow tools for large-scale complete operations, and documents credential-scoped MCP permissions and hidden API keys after setup.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is a concrete practice source for context-window failure modes, tool-vs-API selection, unattended workflow caution, credential-scoped permissions, and avoiding confident partial-data actions.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate evidence for codebase/source ingest pages that distinguish bounded agent context from complete dataset operations.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, avoid restating Ontraport product setup; extract the generic practice rule.

items.source_title: The hidden bill behind agentic AI - and where to run it to maintain control
items.short_factual_summary: A sponsored Business Insider/Dell article frames agentic AI cost as variable consumption driven by repeated context, planning, checking, and revision loops, and argues for workload placement decisions that combine local execution, policy rules, action logs, and cloud escalation for frontier models.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The practice implication is cost-per-outcome governance: agent loops should be budgeted by task shape and context replay, with run-location decisions and logs designed before broad rollout.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate support for hybrid agent infrastructure economics and agent-cost telemetry pages; mark as sponsored source if ingested.
follow_up_notes: Use cautiously because the page is sponsored by Dell AI Factory with Nvidia.

items.source_title: AI safety researchers face shrinking testing windows, rising costs
items.date_basis: News result and article URL show July 24, 2026.
items.short_factual_summary: Axios reports that AI safety and security evaluators face short access windows, high benchmark costs, model test-gaming behavior, benchmark saturation, and calls for earlier testing during training rather than only pre-deployment.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: For local eval practice, it reinforces that agent and model verification gates should use fresh, hard-to-game tasks, monitor sandbox behavior, and avoid treating late-stage pass/fail benchmarks as complete evidence.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate evidence for evaluation-window design, sandbox monitoring, and anti-gaming checks in AI-assisted development verification.
follow_up_notes: Route broad frontier-model safety coverage upstream; keep local synthesis to software-engineering eval governance.

items.short_factual_summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 and describes stronger coding and verification behavior plus beta API features for mid-conversation tool changes without invalidating prompt cache and automatic fallbacks for safety-classifier-blocked requests.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local signal is runtime tool-surface management: changing tools during a run affects cache, permission, and replay assumptions, while fallback routing needs auditability when safety classifiers change execution paths.
items.local_practice_implication: Possible downstream lens for tool-list mutation, prompt-cache assumptions, verification claims, and fallback routing governance.
follow_up_notes: Route broad model release facts upstream; keep only tool-change and fallback governance implications locally.

items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The practice implication is that AI-assisted development risk controls must cover agent workstations, package installation, IDE extensions, CI egress, pull requests, and default branches rather than only generated code review.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate source for package-install risk, agent workstation policy, and CI/CD egress governance pages.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, separate vendor product claims from general software supply-chain practice.
